bannedNote.en: Penalised in competition: current IJF rules answer any grip, block or push on the leg with the hand or arm with a shido, and taking both legs at once is the plainest case of it. Nothing restricts the technique outside contest, and the BJA sets it as a 5th Dan fundamental skill.

note.en: Taking both legs with the hands draws a shido. Nothing about the throw itself is barred; it is the hands reaching the legs that the rule answers.

about.en: The two-handed leg reap: tori drops under the grips, wraps both hands behind uke's knees and drives through with the shoulder, taking both legs away. A Kodokan-recognised te-waza and a staple of wrestling and BJJ, it draws a shido in current IJF competition under the leg-grab rules, but remains legal to practise, appears in older and junior syllabuses, and is essential to recognise and defend.

en: Change levels first: bend the knees, not the back
Both hands behind the knees, shoulder tight to the body
Drive through with the legs; pull the knees towards you
From your own grips or as your partner reaches, bend both knees sharply so your head comes below their chest; keep your back straight.
Step your right foot between their feet and drive forward, placing your right shoulder against their stomach or chest.
Wrap both hands behind their knees, one behind each, palms pulling towards you.
Drive forward and up with your legs while your hands pull their knees past your hips.
Their legs come away and they fall onto their back; keep your head up and to the side, and lower them under control rather than spiking them.
Note for competition: this technique is banned in current IJF contest rules; practise it for grading, ne-waza entries and defence.

receiving.en: The warning is your partner's level dropping suddenly: their head leaves your upper zone and a shoulder plants into your middle, then both your knees are pulled forward while the shoulder keeps driving. Both legs go at once, so the fall is flat onto the back with little time to step out. Neither arm is held, so slap with both, chin tucked hard because the drive can carry you quickly. In practice, agree the pace first; taken gently it is a soft, flat landing.

viNotes.en: VI judo contests start gripped up, which removes the shooting entry this throw is best known for; from contact it becomes a level-change you feel through the grips as your partner's arms drop away. Defending it is mostly tactile: the instant the head drops and a shoulder touches your middle, sprawl your hips back and take the head.

cue.en: Both hands wrap behind the opponent's knees and the shoulder drives through: the double-leg takedown.
